summary.intent: Execute Phase 20 (vault-migration) of the cipher-box project, implementing a v2 binary vault blob format across the TypeScript core, API, Rust desktop, and web client, with lazy migration for existing users.
summary.outcome: Phase 20 completed successfully — all 4 plans executed, 6/6 VAULT requirements verified, PR #344 created and all CodeRabbit/Copilot review comments resolved. Several bugs discovered during UAT were fixed, including v2 blob handling in folder sync, recovery tool IPNS resolution, and two HIGH security issues.

repo: The vault migration worked silently — NestJS does not auto-log incoming request routes, so POST /vault/migrate appeared to never be called when it actually succeeded at 00:12:38 UTC

orval v7.18.0 generates `{ [key: string]: unknown } | null` for nullable string fields even when the OpenAPI spec correctly has `type: string, nullable: true` — requires `as unknown as string` casts in useAuth.ts as workaround
The IPFS gateway at 192.168.133.114:8080 supports CORS (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`) but the Kubo API on port 5001 does not, making browser-side IPNS resolution via the API port impossible
The IPFS gateway supports `/ipns/{name}` path resolution directly and returns `X-Ipfs-Roots` header with the resolved CID — this is more reliable for recovery tool use than delegated routing APIs
Subfolder IPNS records are only stored in the CipherBox API's DB cache and are not propagated to the public DHT, so recovery tool subfolder traversal fails on public infra
The Rust desktop code predates the SDK extraction (phase 19.1) and duplicates crypto/IPNS/metadata logic that now lives in @cipherbox/core and @cipherbox/sdk-core
The NestJS IPNS controller requires JWT auth — the recovery tool cannot use it as a fallback without credentials

code.finding: fetchAndDecryptMetadata blindly JSON.parsed IPFS blobs without detecting v2 binary format — caused `SyntaxError: Unexpected token` when migration wrote a v2 blob to IPNS
Same v2 blob detection bug as folder.service.ts — also needed the detectBlobVersion + deserialize guard
fetchFromIpfs returned undefined on non-200/non-404 status (e.g., 502/503), causing detectBlobVersion to crash with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')`
serialize_vault_blob_v2 originally returned Vec<u8> without bounds checking — changed to Result to surface u16 key length overflow (HIGH security issue H-1)
InitVaultRequest and VaultResponse derived Debug, leaking encrypted key material in logs — fixed with custom Debug impls that redact sensitive fields (HIGH security issue H-2)
Migration IIFE called deriveVaultIpnsKeypair() twice with identical inputs and had redundant object wrapper for ipnsKeypair — fixed by hoisting derivation and passing directly
Test for getVault missing migratedAt: null in expected DTO shape — caused CI failure after VaultResponseDto was updated

workflow: The classifyHandoffIfNeeded Claude Code runtime bug fires in the completion handler after all tool calls finish — spot-checking SUMMARY.md existence and git commits is the correct way to determine actual success
When debugging 'silent failures', check the database directly before assuming an operation never ran — API logs without request logging middleware are insufficient evidence
The security:review skill is effective for catching issues before verification — running it during the checkpoint pause rather than after saved a verification cycle
Playwright browser_evaluate can extract sensitive in-memory values (like private keys) from running dev sessions for testing purposes

Recovery tool testing requires a non-trivial setup: the private key must be extracted from the Zustand store via Playwright, and IPNS resolution requires the local IPFS gateway path rather than delegated routing APIs

friction: API error 'ConnectionRefused' during the security review caused the first invocation to fail silently, requiring a second attempt
NestJS does not log incoming requests by default, making the POST /vault/migrate call invisible in server logs — caused a lengthy debug session to confirm the migration had already succeeded
The Kubo API (port 5001) lacks CORS headers, blocking browser-side IPNS resolution and forcing a workaround through the IPFS gateway /ipns/ path

orval v7.18.0 generates incorrect TypeScript types for nullable string fields despite a correct OpenAPI spec — the `as unknown as string` casts are a permanent workaround with no clean upstream fix to reference

The recovery tool went through 6 iterations of IPNS resolution approaches (delegated routing → ipfs.io fallback → Kubo API → CipherBox API proxy → CipherBox API 401 → gateway /ipns/ path) before finding one that worked
PR merge conflicts in ROADMAP.md and STATE.md required manual resolution
pnpm dev was backgrounded by the user rather than by Claude, causing task ID tracking to be slightly awkward
open_items: Phase 23 added: Rust SDK Extraction — extract cipherbox-core Rust crate mirroring @cipherbox/core and @cipherbox/sdk-core, with platform-specific plans for macOS (FUSE-T SMB), Linux (kernel FUSE), Windows (WinFSP)

Todo: fix device registry sync fails with 'CryptoError: Invalid registry format' — schema mismatch between current device registry format and IPFS-stored data
Todo: fix bin IPNS name 404 resolution failure

Security medium issues documented but not fixed: M-1 recovery tool private key not zeroed after use, M-2 no dedup guard for concurrent migration from multiple tabs, M-3 unnecessary ECIES re-wrap on every root folder publish
Security low issues documented but not fixed: L-1 zero-length key accepted by deserializers, L-2 no SRI hashes on CDN scripts in recovery.html
Subfolder IPNS records are not propagated to the public DHT — recovery tool subfolder traversal fails for records only in CipherBox API DB cache

Rust commands/vault.rs (41 lines), fuse/mod.rs (25 lines), api/types.rs (17 lines), fuse/decrypt.rs (7 lines) remain at 0% test coverage — requires a Rust integration test framework with running API + IPFS + FUSE
